passages.title: Seeing-eye Dogs
passages.intro: 5 sentences have been removed. Choose the sentence that best fits each gap. There is one extra sentence you do not need.
passages.credit: Original text written for this practice.
paragraphs: Some dogs have a very important job: they help people who are blind or cannot see well. [[1]]
Training starts when the dogs are puppies. They live with a volunteer family for about a year. [[2]] They are taken on buses and trains, to shops and to busy streets.

When they are older, the dogs go to a special school. There, they learn to stop at kerbs and steps, and to walk around things in the way. [[3]] If its owner tells it to cross a road when a car is coming, the dog will not move.
[[4]] Its owner must not pat it or talk to it in a silly voice while it is working. That is why you should always ask before patting a dog in a harness.
At the end of the day, the harness comes off. [[5]] Most seeing-eye dogs love to play, chase balls and snooze on the couch, just like any other dog.

bank.A: Then the dog is just a pet again.
bank.B: They even learn when NOT to obey a command.
bank.C: They are called seeing-eye dogs or guide dogs.
bank.D: Cats can also be trained to do tricks.
bank.E: The family teaches them good manners and helps them get used to noisy places.
bank.F: A guide dog wearing its harness is concentrating hard.
